description: THE CANDIDATE: the release candidate under diagnosis is a values overlay in Git (fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml), not whatever happens to be on main — so the diagnosis is reproducible whichever repairs you have already merged
APP HEALTH: the orders-api process serves /healthz (and /readyz) but has NO /health route — so a probe pointed at /health gets a 404, not because the app is down
command: grep -Eq '@router.get\("/healthz"\)' app/orders-api/src/health.py && ! grep -Eq '@router.get\("/health"\)' app/orders-api/src/health.py && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROBE CONFIG: the candidate's RENDERED readiness probe points at /health — the path the app does not serve — so the pod will never report Ready
command: [ -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 readinessProbe | grep -Eq 'path: /health$' && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROBE CONFIG: the candidate leaves the liveness probe on /healthz — this is the misleading part, the container is NOT killed, it just stays perpetually unready
command: [ -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 livenessProbe | grep -Eq 'path: /healthz$' && echo pass || echo fail

description: ROLLOUT STATE: the candidate renders maxUnavailable as 100% — a rolling update may take every old pod down before a new one is Ready, turning an unready rollout into a full outage
command: [ -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml 2>/dev/null | grep -Eq 'maxUnavailable: 100%' && echo pass || echo fail

description: THE FIX: the defect lives in the candidate's Helm values (desired state in Git), not in the app or the cluster — so the repair is a values change rejected before merge, not a kubectl edit after it
command: grep -Eq 'path: /health *$' fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml && echo pass || echo fail

description: THE REGRESSION: main's committed readiness probe is a route the app actually serves — which is what makes the candidate a REGRESSION rather than a pre-existing bug, and why the diff is the thing to review
command: p=$(helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | awk '/readinessProbe:/{f=1} f&&/path:/{print $2; exit}'); [ -n "$p" ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; grep -Eq "@router.get\\(\"$p\"\\)" app/orders-api/src/health.py && echo pass || echo fail

description: THE FIX VERIFIED: dropping the candidate's probe override renders a readiness probe that matches a route the app really serves (proven with helm template, no cluster touched)
command:
f=$(mktemp); printf 'readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: http
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
' > "$f"; helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api -f fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml -f "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 readinessProbe | grep -Eq 'path: /healthz$' && echo pass || echo fail; rm -f "$f"

description: GOVERNANCE: the repair path is the golden path — a direct kubectl edit of the live deployment from an agent identity is exactly the wrong-target class the gate blocks; the fix is proposed in Git
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"kubectl edit deployment orders-api -A"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail
